sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... AN AMPLIFIED BUT RELATIVELY PROGRESSIVE LARGE SCALE PATTERN WILL EXIST OVER THE CONUS. THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN PLAINS UPPER RIDGE WILL SHIFT EASTWARD TOWARD THE OZARKS/MS RIVER VALLEY TODAY...WHILE A CLOSED UPPER LOW CURRENTLY OVER THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST OPENS/ACCELERATES EASTWARD OVER THE NORTHERN ROCKIES.

sections.title: MT/EASTERN WY TO THE DAKOTAS/MN
sections.text: STEADY HEIGHT FALLS ARE EXPECTED ACROSS THE MAJORITY OF THE REGION IN ADVANCE OF THE NORTHERN ROCKIES UPPER TROUGH...COINCIDENT WITH A SOUTHEASTWARD MOVING NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS COLD FRONT AND NORTH-CENTRAL PLAINS SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS /PRINCIPALLY ACROSS SD/. INITIAL SURFACE BASED TSTM DEVELOPMENT SHOULD OCCUR THIS AFTERNOON WITHIN A CORRIDOR FROM EAST-CENTRAL MT INTO EASTERN WY/SD BLACK HILLS VICINITY. THE STORMS ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL MT WILL BE WITHIN A MORE MARGINAL BUOYANCY/VERTICAL SHEAR REGIME IMMEDIATELY AHEAD OF THE UPPER LOW...BUT THE STRONGEST OF THE LOW-TOPPED STORMS WILL NONETHELESS BE CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL/GUSTY WINDS. MORE VIGOROUS STORM DEVELOPMENT IS PROBABLE ACROSS THE NORTH-CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS IN THE NORTHWEST QUADRANT OF THE AFOREMENTIONED SURFACE LOW AND NEAR/BEHIND A COLD FRONT AND/OR INVERTED TROUGH. ON THE NORTHERN FRINGES OF A SUBSTANTIAL ELEVATED MIXED LAYER/CAP...AND SOUTH OF MORE PREVALENT CLOUD COVER/PRECIPITATION ACROSS ND...THE BOUNDARY LAYER WILL BECOME MODERATELY UNSTABLE /MLCAPE 1500+ J PER KG/ BY PEAK HEATING ESPECIALLY ACROSS SD AND ADJACENT PARTS OF FAR SOUTHERN ND AND FAR EASTERN WY/SOUTHEAST MT. AIDED BY STRENGTHENING SOUTHWESTERLY FLOW ALOFT...V

sections.title: MIDWEST/MIDDLE MS VALLEY
sections.text: AS A FRONTAL BOUNDARY CONTINUES TO SAG SOUTHWARD...TSTMS MAY PERSIST/REDEVELOP AND POSSIBLY BECOME SURFACE BASED LATER TODAY WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR. VERTICAL SHEAR/OVERALL FORCING WILL BE WEAK ON THE EASTERN PERIPHERY OF AN APPROACHING UPPER RIDGE...BUT POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING/DESTABILIZATION MAY ALLOW FOR A FEW STRONGER STORMS CAPABLE OF DOWNBURSTS THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. ..GUYER/DEAN.. 09/08/2013

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PARTS OF THE NRN PLNS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... RIDGE CENTERED OVER THE CNTRL PLNS WILL EDGE E/SE INTO THE OZARKS/LWR MS VLY THIS PERIOD AS WA/ID UPR LOW ACCELERATES E ACROSS MT IN RESPONSE TO PROGRESSIVE SYSTEM NOW ENTERING NRN BC. ELSEWHERE...WEAKER...CONVECTIVELY-ENHANCED DISTURBANCES...SHOULD CONTINUE TO ROTATE AROUND THE NWRN AND NERN FLANKS OF THE PLNS RIDGE. AT THE SFC...EXPECT EXISTING LEE LOW NOW OVER WRN NEB/SD TO BEGIN MOVING ENE TOWARD MN LATER TODAY/TNGT. ASSOCIATED WARM/STNRY FRONT SHOULD SERVE AS THE MAIN FOCUS FOR STRONG TO SVR TSTMS THIS PERIOD...MAINLY OVER THE NRN PLNS. OTHER STRONG TO POSSIBLY SVR STORMS MAY OCCUR FARTHER W OVER PARTS OF MT/NRN WY...CLOSER TO EJECTING UPR LOW.

sections.title: MT/NE WY INTO DAKOTAS/MN TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: LOW-LVL CONVERGENCE SHOULD FOCUS/STRENGTHEN OVER WRN/NRN SD AND SRN ND LATER TODAY/TNGT AS UPR LOW/TROUGH CROSSING MT GRADUALLY ENHANCES LARGE SCALE ASCENT AND MID/UPR-LVL FLOW ACROSS REGION. LOW-LVL UPLIFT SHOULD FOCUS ALONG SYNOPTIC WARM/STNRY FRONT EXTENDING ROUGHLY ESE FROM NW NEB SFC LOW. ALTHOUGH THE BOUNDARY IS DIFFUSE ATTM AND THE SFC PATTERN IS COMPLICATED BY OUTFLOW FROM ON-GOING NRN SD MCS...THE FRONT SHOULD BECOME BETTER-DEFINED BY MID-LATE AFTN AS IT REFORMS NWD INTO CNTRL SD. COMBINATION OF SFC HEATING...RICH MOISTURE /PW AROUND 1.75 IN/...AND DEEP EML SHOULD YIELD STRONG INSTABILITY INVOF THE FRONT...WITH POCKETS OF MLCAPE AOA 2500 J/KG POSSIBLE BY LATE IN THE DAY. COUPLED WITH 35-40 SWLY DEEP SHEAR/VERTICALLY-VEERING WIND PROFILES...SETUP COULD SUPPORT A FEW SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...LOCALLY DMGG WIND...AND A COUPLE TORNADOES. MORE WDLY SCTD STORMS WITH SVR WIND/HAIL MAY EXTEND SW ALONG LEE TROUGH INTO ERN WY/WRN SD AND NW NEB. CONTINUED EWD ADVANCE OF MT UPR LOW SHOULD SUPPORT A MORE SUBSTANTIAL NOCTURNALLY-ENHANCED SSWLY LLJ OVER THE NRN PLNS TNGT/EARLY MON THAN HAS BEEN THE CASE IN RECENT DAYS. THIS MAY FOSTER STORM MERGERS/UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A FORWARD

sections.title: OZARKS/MID MS VLY THIS AFTN/EVE
sections.text: ERN EXTENSION OF PLNS WARM/STNRY FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE SLOWLY S/SW OVER PARTS OF THE LWR OH AND MID MS VLY TODAY AS SFC HIGH BUILDS SE ACROSS THE GRT LKS. THE BOUNDARY WILL BE AUGMENTED IN IL/MO BY OUTFLOW FROM OVERNIGHT STORMS. THE FRONT SHOULD SERVE AS A FOCUS FOR RENEWED TSTM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTN AS SFC HEATING BENEATH ERN FRINGE OF PLNS EML BOOSTS SBCAPE TO 1500-2000 J/KG. VERTICAL SHEAR AND LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE FAIRLY WEAK. BUT STRONG BUOYANCY MAY SUPPORT A FEW PULSE AND/OR MULTICELL STORMS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DMGG WIND THIS AFTN THROUGH EARLY EVE. ..CORFIDI/BOTHWELL.. 09/08/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AN UPPER HIGH CENTERED OVER THE CNTRL PLAINS WILL SHIFT EWD INTO THE OZARKS IN RESPONSE TO THE EWD PROGRESSION OF AN UPPER LOW FROM THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION INTO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. THIS PATTERN EVOLUTION WILL RESULT IN STRENGTHENING LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT AND MID AND UPPER-LEVEL FLOW FROM THE NRN HIGH PLAINS TOWARD UPPER MS VALLEY. IN THE LOW LEVELS...A LEE CYCLONE OVER NWRN NEB WILL DEEPEN WHILE DEVELOPING INTO NERN SD BY 9/12Z. AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE FRONT CURRENTLY EXTENDING FROM THE LOW ESEWD THROUGH ERN NEB...SRN IA INTO THE OH VALLEY WILL LIFT NWD IN RESPONSE TO A STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME DOWNSTREAM FROM THE MIGRATORY CYCLONE. MEANWHILE...A DEVELOPING PACIFIC FRONT FROM THE NRN ROCKIES INTO GREAT BASIN WILL ADVANCE EWD THROUGH WRN PARTS OF THE DAKOTAS AND NEB BY THE END OF THE FORECAST PERIOD.

sections.title: PARTS OF MT/WY INTO THE DAKOTAS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: 12Z SOUNDINGS AND SATELLITE-DERIVED PW IMAGERY SHOW THE CONTINUED PRESENCE OF A SEASONABLY MOIST AIR MASS INVOF OF STALLED SYNOPTIC FRONT WITH BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S TO LOWER 70S AND PW VALUES OF 1.2-1.8 INCHES. DECREASING MORNING CLOUDINESS COUPLED WITH THIS HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 1000-1500 J/KG OVER MT TO AS HIGH AS 2000-3000 J/KG ACROSS SD. CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION WILL BE DICTATED TO SOME DEGREE BY THE AREAL COVERAGE AND EXTENT OF LINGERING CLOUDS. BUT IN GENERAL...IT APPEARS THAT HEATING ALONG THE ELEVATED TERRAIN OF MT...WY...AND WRN SD...ALONG WITH INCREASING CONVERGENCE INVOF THE SYNOPTIC LOW AND NWD-DEVELOPING WARM FRONT WILL BE THE PRIMARY FOCI FOR STRONG TO SEVERE TSTM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF A VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILE AND STRENGTHENING MID TO UPPER-LEVEL FLOW --AND RESULTANT VERTICAL SHEAR-- INITIAL STORM MODE WILL LIKELY BE SUPERCELLULAR WITH A RISK FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND PERHAPS A BRIEF TORNADO. AGGREGATING STORM-SCALE COLD POOLS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NOCTURNAL LOW-LEVEL WIND MA

sections.title: OZARKS THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY EVENING
sections.text: WEAK LOW-LEVEL WAA IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST TODAY...ENHANCING INFLOW/ASCENT ALONG THE WRN FLANK OF NOCTURNAL MCS ONGOING ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL MO. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT REGENERATIVE STORM DEVELOPMENT ON THE WRN END OF THE RESIDUAL MCS WHERE DAYTIME HEATING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS OF 65-70 F WILL PROMOTE MLCAPE APPROACHING 1500-2500+ J/KG. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN RATHER WEAK...LIMITING THE POTENTIAL FOR STORM ORGANIZATION. NONETHELESS...LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE OWING TO THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY AND HIGH PW ENVIRONMENT. ..MEAD/LEITMAN.. 09/08/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS PORTIONS OF CNTRL AND SRN MT...AS WELL AS PARTS OF NRN AND ERN WY...THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. A SEVERE TSTM WATCH MAY BE NEED IN THE NEXT HOUR OR SO FOR SOME OF THESE AREAS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AIRMASS ALONG STALLED FRONTAL SEGMENT SITUATED FROM SERN MT NWWD INTO CNTRL PORTIONS OF THE STATE HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE WITH SBCAPE NOW ESTIMATED TO AROUND 1000 J PER KG. MEANWHILE...STORMS HAVE BEEN INCREASING IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY WITHIN A BAND OF STRONGER DEEP-LAYER ASCENT ACCOMPANYING AN EJECTING SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS NWRN MT. GIVEN CONTINUED HEATING ACROSS THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF MT AND WY...COINCIDENT WITH STRENGTHENING DEEP-LAYER ASCENT WITH THE UPPER TROUGH AND ALONG THE FRONT...REMAINING INHIBITION SHOULD GIVE WAY TO NUMEROUS STORMS DEVELOPING OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. A COMPACT BELT OF STRONGER CYCLONIC MID-LEVEL FLOW OF 30-40KT WILL SPREAD EAST WITH THE EJECTING MID/UPPER TROUGH AMIDST THE DEVELOPING CONVECTION. THIS SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO ENHANCED EFFECTIVE SHEAR AND THE POSSIBILITY OF A FEW SUPERCELLS AND/OR LINE SEGMENTS EVOLVING WITH AN INCREASING CHANCE FOR HIGH WINDS AND LARGE HAIL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED INTENSE TSTMS WITH SOME POSSIBILITY OF DOWNBURST WINDS AND MARGINAL HAIL MAY DRIFT SOUTH ALONG THE MO/KS BORDER IN THE VICINITY OF KANSAS CITY OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. STORM COVERAGE/DURATION MAY NOT RISE TO THE LEVEL WHERE A WATCH IS NEEDED BUT THE AREA WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED DEVELOPMENT NEAR STJ OVER THE PAST HOUR OR SO APPEARS TO BE THE RESULT OF INTENSE SURFACE HEATING CONTRIBUTING TO LOCAL REMOVAL OF STRONG CAPPING INVERSION AND PERHAPS GLANCING INFLUENCE FROM REMNANT MCV ACROSS ERN MO. WITH SURFACE TEMPERATURES ACROSS ERN KS AND THE MKC AREA CLIMBING INTO THE 100-105F RANGE...MOST INHIBITION EXHIBITED ON MORNING SOUNDING FROM TOP IS REMOVED AND MLCAPE VALUES BECOME QUITE HIGH AROUND 3000 J/KG. WITH 40F SFC DEWPOINT DEPRESSIONS AND DCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 1000 J/KG...ANY CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT WILL POSE A THREAT FOR DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS. GREATEST LIMITATION IN STORM DEVELOPMENT AND COVERAGE WILL LIKELY BE THE LACK OF STRONGER LARGE SCALE FORCING AND SHEAR GIVEN THE REGION LIES ALMOST DIRECTLY BENEATH STRONG ANTICYCLONE WITH MID-LEVEL WINDS AOB 15KT AND WEAKENING. THUS...EXPECT ANY ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT DRIVEN BY DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE TO REMAIN QUITE ISOLATED AND SHORT-LIVED AND A WATCH DOES NOT APPEAR NEEDED FOR THIS ACTIVITY.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST ISOLATED SVR THUNDERSTORMS COULD OCCUR ACROSS PARTS OF THE DAKOTAS AND ADJACENT MT/WY INTO THE EVENING HOURS...AND CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SUGGESTS THAT LITTLE IN THE WAY OF DEEP FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE PRESENT WITHIN A BROAD RIBBON OF ENHANCED MID-LEVEL MOISTURE CRESTING A CNTRL-CONUS RIDGE. ALSO...SFC OBSERVATIONS REVEAL LIMITED CONVERGENCE AMIDST A WEAK-FLOW PATTERN WITHIN A RELATIVELY MOIST -- ALBEIT NOT PARTICULARLY WARM -- AIR MASS LOCATED N OF A WAVY...QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT ANALYZED FROM SRN SD INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE AND ERN WY. THIS IS WHERE THE JUXTAPOSITION OF SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER/MIDDLE 60S WITH TEMPERATURES IN THE MIDDLE 70S TO THE LOWER 80S BENEATH MODESTLY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES IS SUPPORTING MODERATE INSTABILITY. ABUNDANT AREAS OF MULTI-LAYERED CLOUDS HAVE LIMITED DIABATIC SFC HEATING/DESTABILIZATION...AND THERE IS SUBSTANTIAL UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE COVERAGE OF ROBUST CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND ASSOCIATED SVR POTENTIAL. REGARDLESS...SUFFICIENT LOW-LEVEL ASCENT COULD EXIST INVOF ILL-DEFINED BOUNDARIES/WIND-SHIFT AXES/TERRAIN-DRIVEN CIRCULATIONS -- E.G. A WIND-SHIFT AXIS LYING FROM WRN ND TO NERN WY -- FOR AT LEAST ISOLATED DEEP CONVECTION TO CONTINUE INTO THE EVENING HOURS. ALSO...SOME UPTICK IN CONVECTION MAY OCCUR IN ASSOCIATION WITH INCREASING ASCENT WITHIN THE EXIT-REGION OF A NOCTURNALLY STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL JET STREAM OVER THE LOWER PLAINS LATER THIS EVENING. GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF 30-50 KT OF MID-LEVEL FLOW PER AREA VWP DATA...DEEP SHEAR MAY BE SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW SUSTAINED/ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE STRUCTURES...WHICH COULD ALSO SPREAD E OF ONGOING WW 516. A CONDITIONAL POTENTIAL FOR SVR WIND/HAIL MAY OCCUR WITH SUCH ACTIVITY...THOUGH INCREASING NOCTURNAL BOUNDARY-LAYER CINH MAY REDUCE ANY SVR WIND THREAT WITH TIME INTO THE EVENING HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS CENTRAL MT...AND IS SLOWLY SPREADING EWD WITH TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BROKEN LINE OF STRONG/POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS CONTINUES TO EVOLVE ACROSS PARTS OF CENTRAL/N CENTRAL MT...FROM JUST E OF HVR /HAVRE MT/ TO NEAR AND S OF LWT /LEWISTOWN MT/. THE CONVECTION IS EVOLVING WITHIN A BAND OF ASCENT JUST AHEAD OF THE NWRN MT UPPER CIRCULATION CENTER...WHERE A MODESTLY BUOYANT ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY MIXED-LAYER CAPE IN THE 500 TO 1000 J/KG RANGE EXISTS PER OBJECTIVE ANALYSES. REPORTS OF LARGE HAIL HAVE BEEN RECEIVED FROM STORMS WITHIN THIS BAND EARLIER...AND WHILE THREAT FOR HAIL CONTINUES...THE RISK FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS APPEARS TO BE INCREASING LOCALLY AS WELL...CORRESPONDING TO THE INCREASED LINEAR ORGANIZATION OF THE STORMS. THOUGH EWD EXTENT OF THE MAIN AXIS OF INSTABILITY IS LIMITED...SEVERE RISK IS EXPECTED FOR AT LEAST THE NEXT 2-3 HOURS AS CONVECTION CONTINUES SHIFTING EWD. ..GOSS.. 09/08/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: BROKEN LINE OF STORMS CONTINUES TO PROGRESS EWD TOWARD ERN MT...WITH ONGOING/ISOLATED SEVERE RISK.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS AN ARCING/LOOSELY ORGANIZED LINE OF STORMS CONTINUING EWD ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN MT...WITH THE STRONGEST CONVECTION NOW AFFECTING MUSSELSHELL/PETROLEUM/WRN GARFIELD COUNTIES. OTHER/ISOLATED STORMS ARE ALSO ONGOING ACROSS SRN PORTIONS OF THE WW...AND ISOLATED SEVERE POTENTIAL CONTINUES ACROSS THE VALID PORTIONS OF THE WATCH. WITH TIME HOWEVER...STORMS SHOULD EXHIBIT A SLOW DECREASE IN INTENSITY...DUE TO A COMBINATION OF THE LOSS OF DIURNAL HEATING AND STORMS SHIFTING E OF THE AXIS OF GREATER INSTABILITY. AS SUCH...THE NEED FOR AN ADDITIONAL WW E OF THE CURRENT WATCH INTO E CENTRAL AND NERN MT APPEARS UNNECESSARY ATTM. IN THE MEAN TIME...THREAT FOR MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL AND/OR WIND GUSTS SHOULD PERSIST OVER THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS. ..GOSS.. 09/09/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STORMS CONTINUE MOVING EWD ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS EVENING. WHILE STORMS IN GENERAL HAVE REMAINED SUB-SEVERE RECENTLY...THREAT FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL CONTINUES.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS A LOOSELY ORGANIZED N-S BAND OF STORMS MOVING OUT OF ERN WY/SERN MT INTO SWRN ND AND WRN SD...WITH THE MOST ORGANIZED ZONE OF CONVECTION -- IN THE FORM OF AN ARCING BAND -- NOW CROSSING THE BLACK HILLS. THREAT FOR LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL CONTINUES -- PARTICULARLY WITH THIS CLUSTER OF STORMS. CONVECTION WILL CONTINUE MOVING EWD WITH TIME...THROUGH A WRN SD AIRMASS FEATURING AN INCREASINGLY CAPPED BOUNDARY LAYER -- SUGGESTING THAT DAMAGING WIND THREAT MAY REMAIN LIMITED. HAVING SAID THAT...OBJECTIVE ANALYSES AND EVENING ABR RAOB BOTH INDICATE AN AXIS OF GREATER BUOYANCY OVER CENTRAL AND ERN SD...AND WEAKER CAPPING AS WELL OWING TO A VERY MOIST /UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S DEWPOINTS/ BOUNDARY LAYER. AS A SLY LOW-LEVEL JET HELPS TO SUSTAIN THE EWD-MOVING STORM CLUSTER...THE MORE FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT MAY ALLOW SEVERE RISK TO LINGER INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS. WITH EVOLUTION STILL UNCERTAIN...CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS WITH RESPECT TO ANY LINGERING/DOWNSTREAM SEVERE RISK BEYOND THAT CONTAINED WITHIN WW 517. ..GOSS.. 09/09/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR ADDITIONAL SVR TSTM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF WW 517 CONTINUES TO DIMINISH. AN ADDITIONAL WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED AFTER EXPIRATION AT 07Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTM COMPLEX HAS MOVED INTO WRN PORTIONS OF RECENTLY ISSUED WW 518...AND THE AIR MASS OVER REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF WW 517 HAS STABILIZED AS A RESULT OF WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW. WITH THE STRONGEST LOW-LEVEL WARM/MOIST ADVECTION EXPECTED TO REMAIN CONFINED TO CENTRAL/ERN SD FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS...AN ADDITIONAL WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED FOR REMAINING VALID PORTIONS OF WW 517.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE THREAT FOR SVR WX ASSOCIATED WITH A WELL-DEVELOPED BOWING SEGMENT CONTINUES ACROSS ERN PORTIONS WW 518. A NEW WW MAY BE NEEDED FARTHER EAST...AND CONVECTIVE TRENDS CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A WELL-DEVELOPED BOWING LINE OF SVR TSTMS CONTINUES TO MOVE NEWD AT 45 KTS ACROSS N-CENTRAL SD/ADJACENT S-CENTRAL ND. AT 0745Z THE LEADING EDGE EXTENDED FROM LOGAN COUNTY ND SWD INTO EDMUNDS COUNTY SD...WITH A RECENT SPOTTER REPORT OF 60 TO 70 MPH WINDS. RADAR DATA FROM KABR AND KBIS SHOWS A PRONOUNCED/STRONG REAR-INFLOW JET AND WELL-DEVELOPED COLD POOL WITH THIS CONVECTIVE SYSTEM. MESOANALYSIS AND VWP DATA FROM KABR SHOWS STRONG LOW-LEVEL WAA DOWNSTREAM FROM THE LINE OF TSTMS AIDED BY 45-50 KT LOW-LEVEL JET...AND LATEST RUC GUIDANCE INDICATES INCREASING WAA INTO PORTIONS OF CENTRAL MN IN THE 09-12Z TIME FRAME. THE AIR MASS OVER SERN ND/NERN SD REMAINS MODERATELY UNSTABLE WITH MUCAPES OF 1000-2000 J/KG...WITH DIMINISHING VALUES FARTHER E INTO W-CENTRAL MN. AN ADDITIONAL WW IS POSSIBLE TO THE E OF WW 518 PRIOR TO 09Z...ALTHOUGH IT REMAINS UNCLEAR JUST HOW FAR E INTO WRN MN THE SVR THREAT WILL EXIST.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG/DAMAGING WIND THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS ERN PORTIONS OF WW...BUT WILL CONTINUE TO BECOME MORE ISOLATED WITH TIME AND LIKELY SHIFT TO SRN PORTION OF CONVECTIVE LINE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BOWING LINE OF SVR TSTMS HAS RECENTLY SHOWN RADAR-BASED SIGNS OF WEAKENING SINCE 0930Z...ALTHOUGH ISOLATED STRONG/SVR GUSTS MAY STILL OCCUR AS THE WELL-DEVELOPED COMMA HEAD AND REAR INFLOW JET SLOWLY WEAKEN. AS THE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM CONTINUES MOVING NEWD...IT ENCOUNTERS A PROGRESSIVELY COOLER BOUNDARY LAYER AND WITH DIMINISHING MUCAPE /AVERAGING 500 TO 1000 J/KG/. IN ADDITION...A VEERING LOW-LEVEL JET HAS REFOCUSED WAA TO ALONG THE SRN PERIPHERY OF THE CONVECTIVE LINE...WHERE TSTMS HAVE STRENGTHENED SINCE 09Z. CURRENT INDICATIONS ARE THE SVR THREAT SHOULD BE GREATEST IN THIS AREA...AFFECTING GRANT AND OTTER TAIL COUNTIES IN WRN MN.
